chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Bayhaqi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Sawli informed us. He said: Abu Dhakwan narrated to us. He said: I heard Ibrahim ibn al-Abbas say:
I have never seen al-Rida (peace be upon him) asked about anything except that he knew it. I have never seen anyone more knowledgeable than him about what had occurred in time up to his era and age.
Al-Ma'mun would test him by asking about everything, and he would answer on it. All his speech, his answers, and his illustrations were with verses from the Quran.

He would complete it every three days, and he would say: Had I wanted to complete it in fewer than three days, I would have done so. However, I never pass by a verse without contemplating it — what it was revealed about, and at what time — and for that reason I have come to complete it in three days.

key_terms.الرضا: Al-Rida — Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (AS), the eighth Imam
key_terms.المأمون: Al-Ma'mun — Abbasid Caliph who invited Imam al-Rida to Khorasan and designated him as crown prince
key_terms.فكّر: To contemplate/reflect deeply — used here for meditative pondering on Quranic revelation
key_terms.يختمه: Completing the recitation — khatm al-Quran, completing the full recitation of the Quran

ai.seo_question: What did witnesses say about Imam al-Rida's knowledge of the Quran?
ai.summary: Ibrahim ibn al-Abbas, a close companion and court secretary who witnessed Imam al-Rida (AS) during his time in Khorasan at the Abbasid court of al-Ma'mun, testifies to the Imam's extraordinary knowledge. He describes how the Imam always knew the answer to any question, surpassed all contemporaries in learning, used Quranic verses for all discourse, and recited the entire Quran in three days — not due to limitation but because of his deep meditative reflection on the occasion, context, and meaning of every verse. This hadith is significant as it comes from a non-partisan Abbasid source (al-Sawli and Ibrahim), lending it particular credibility.
